newsitem.title: MEXICO: Phelps Dodge to open $42 mln Mexico plant.
newsitem.headline: Phelps Dodge to open $42 mln Mexico plant.

text.p: Phelps Dodge division Phelps Dodge Magnet Wire de Mexico placed the first stone Wednesday of a $42 million plant in a suburb 34 km outside this northern industrial center.

"The $42 million investment will allow the company to tend to the growing maquiladora demand for magnetic wire," president of the U.S.-based Phelps Dodge Magnet Wire Company Kirk Kemmish said in a brief ceremony.
Kemmish said the plant will begin operations in January 1998 and will have a capacity of 35,000 tons of magnetic wire per year. Magnetic wire is a conductor used in most electrical systems.

Previously much of the wire used in Mexico's maquiladora, or in-bond, industry was made in Phelps Dodge's plants in Texas. Copper for the wires will still be imported from the United States, but Kemmish said the possibility of buying Mexican copper will be studied in 1998.
The company's Mexico plant is expected to generate 140 jobs.
"The maquiladora market is hoped to grow 10 percent from 1995 to 2000. In addition Monterrey has excellent infrastructure and a skilled labor force," Kemmish said.
